name: Iran APT39 — Remix Kitten / Chafer
author: Threat Intelligence Team
prerequisites: Email server logs (Exchange, O365) with mail flow details available
Proxy and web gateway logs with full URI and user-agent
File server and SharePoint/OneDrive access logs in SIEM
User behavior baseline for data access volumes
required_tools: Microsoft 365 Compliance Center for mail and file access audit
Splunk with Exchange, proxy, file access, and endpoint logs
DLP platform for data staging and exfil detection
Zeek or Arkime for C2 traffic analysis

hunt_actions.title: Email and PII Data Collection (APT39 Focus)
actions: Hunt for bulk email collection from Exchange or O365 (APT39 specifically targets PII for surveillance purposes): `Search-UnifiedAuditLog -RecordType ExchangeItem -Operations Copy,Move,HardDelete,SendAs -StartDate '2025-01-01' -EndDate '2025-04-01' | Where-Object { $_.UserIds -notmatch 'service|system|admin' } | Group-Object UserIds | Sort Count -Desc | Select -First 20`

Detect unauthorized mailbox export (PST/EML export via Compliance Center or MAPI): `Search-UnifiedAuditLog -Operations New-MailboxExportRequest,New-ComplianceSearchAction -StartDate '2025-01-01' | ConvertFrom-Json | Select CreationDate, UserIds, ResultCount, AuditData | Export-Csv mailbox_exports.csv` — any export request not tied to an approved eDiscovery or HR case is a critical finding

hunt_actions.title: SEAWEED, CACHEMONEY, and Custom Implant Detection
actions: Hunt for SEAWEED backdoor (HTTP-based RAT, uses HTTP GET with encoded params): `index=proxy cs-method=GET cs-uri-query=*id=* AND cs-uri-query=*cmd=* | stats count by src_ip, cs-uri-stem, cs-uri-query | sort -count` — SEAWEED uses predictable GET parameter patterns; also look for: responses with Content-Type text/plain of uniform small size (< 1KB) to the same URI repeatedly

Detect CACHEMONEY credential stealer artifacts: `index=windows EventCode=4688 CommandLine=*cachedump* OR (Image=*fgdump.exe* OR Image=*pwdump*) | table _time, host, SubjectUserName, CommandLine` — CACHEMONEY targets cached Windows credentials; also monitor: `index=windows EventCode=4663 ObjectServer='Security Account Manager' | stats count by SubjectUserName, host`

hunt_actions.title: Data Staging and Exfiltration
actions: Detect data staging in local temp or user directories (APT39 stages compressed archives before exfil): Sysmon Event 11 (File Create): `index=windows EventCode=11 (TargetFilename=*\Temp\*.zip OR TargetFilename=*\Temp\*.rar OR TargetFilename=*\Temp\*.7z OR TargetFilename=*\AppData\*.zip) | stats count by host, TargetFilename, Image | sort -count` — large archive creation in temp directories by non-archival processes is anomalous

Hunt for exfiltration to cloud storage or file sharing services (APT39 uses legitimate services as exfil channels): `index=proxy cs-uri-stem IN (*drive.google.com*,*onedrive.live.com*,*dropbox.com*,*mega.nz*,*wetransfer.com*,*gofile.io*) cs-method=POST | stats sum(sc-bytes) as bytes_sent by src_ip, cs-uri-stem | where bytes_sent > 52428800 | sort -bytes_sent` — > 50MB sent to personal cloud storage from a single host requires investigation

hunt_actions.title: Telecom and Travel Sector Targeting Indicators
actions: Hunt for reconnaissance against internal HR and travel systems (APT39 targets personnel data): `index=webserver cs-uri-stem IN (*hr.*,*travel.*,*payroll.*,*roster.*) cs-method=GET | stats dc(c-ip) as unique_ips, count by cs-uri-stem | where unique_ips > 20 | sort -unique_ips` — unusual numbers of unique IPs accessing HR web portals indicates scanning or unauthorized access

Detect LDAP queries targeting large sets of user objects (APT39 enumerates AD for personnel data): `index=windows EventCode=1644 | rex field=Message 'Filter: (?P<filter>[^\n]+)' | rex field=Message 'Entries Returned: (?P<returned>\d+)' | where tonumber(returned) > 500 | table _time, host, filter, returned` — Event 1644 logs expensive LDAP queries; returning > 500 user objects indicates bulk personnel enumeration

questions: Are mailbox export and eDiscovery search capabilities in Exchange/O365 restricted to a limited set of authorized administrators, and are all export actions logged and reviewed?
Is there a Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy configured to alert on bulk transfer of files containing PII (names, passport numbers, phone numbers, travel records) to external destinations?
Is access to HR systems, personnel rosters, travel booking systems, and payroll databases restricted to need-to-know and monitored for bulk data access or export attempts?
Are outbound connections to personal cloud storage services (Google Drive, Dropbox, Mega.nz, OneDrive personal) blocked or strictly monitored for endpoints handling sensitive personnel data?
Is the organization in a sector historically targeted by APT39 (telecommunications, travel, hospitality, high-tech), and has this been explicitly included in the current threat model?
Are proxy and web gateway logs retaining the full HTTP request URI, user-agent string, and response size for at least 90 days to support retrospective APT39 C2 traffic analysis?
Are Active Directory LDAP query logs (Event 1644, requires LDAP diagnostics enabled) or equivalent telemetry available to detect bulk user object enumeration?
Is there a process to correlate data staging events (large archive creation on endpoints) with subsequent network exfiltration attempts to the same source host within a defined time window?
